items.title: Museums, concert halls and ‘haunted’ estates set to host Halloween events in Mississauga
items.summary: Mississauga residents looking for Halloween activities have several options to choose from this month and into November. From pumpkin carving and petting zoos to spooky attractions and seasonal treats, several events are planned across the city for families and residents of all ages. m. Where: Bradley Museum Visitors can roast marshmallows and make s’mores around a fire pit, visit a petting zoo, enjoy warm apple cider and take part in a scavenger hunt with prizes. Other activities include heritage demonstrations, games, crafts, face painting, live music and scarecrow decorating. The event will also offer samples of freshly churned ice cream in fall flavours such as caramel apple and pumpkin spice. The event is paid, and tickets can be purchased online or on-site at Bradley Museum. On-site payments are accepted by credit or debit card. The festival will take place regardless of the weather. m.

items.title: Mississauga's Meadowvale Village Turns 190
items.summary: 2026 marks the 190th anniversary for Meadowvale Village … maybe. The Meadowvale Village Heritage Conservation District is a special place within our city where the treasured heritage landscape is preserved within the wider city that has grown around it. The signs along Old Derry Road proudly announce when you’ve crossed into the historic community and proclaim, “since 1836”. Many stories and published articles on the history of Meadowvale Village provide the establishment date for the village as 1836. The date can be found in the 1904 publication entitled A Souvenir of the Village of Meadowvale-on-the-Credit by Harry Spiers. Another publication, written in 1922 for the Meadowvale Old Home Rally by the Meadowvale Women’s Institute, also references the 1836 founding date. However, neither clarifies its singular importance. MEADOWVALE VILLAGE - 1856 BRISTOW SURVEY. The story of Meadowvale Village begins earlier, shortly following the signing of Treaty 19 between the Indigenous Mississauga and the Crown in 1818. Settlement in the northern area of historic Mississauga, north of what is now Eglinton Avenue, began in earnest after the 1819 survey. At the same time, a group of people living in New York were anxiously looking for a new home in Upper Canada following the War of 1812. Many had grown weary of anti-British sentiment in the years following the war, and no longer felt safe in the United States of America. John Beatty and Joseph Carter, representing the interests of a like-minded group of families, made several trips to York (Toronto) in 1818 and early 1819, seeking suitable land for their group. A petition for land was presented to Lieutenant-Governor Sir Peregrine Maitland on April 22, 1819, on behalf of the group.

items.title: Gardeners Urged to Protect Plants as Frost Warning Hits Toronto, Mississauga and Brampton
items.summary: Insauga.com reports a frost warning is in effect for Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton and surrounding areas as temperatures drop sharply overnight into Saturday morning. According to the outlet, the coldest conditions are expected north of Highway 401, where temperatures could fall to around 0 C, while areas closer to Lake Ontario should stay a few degrees warmer thanks to the lake's moderating effect. The outlet says the sudden cold could damage plants, trees and crops still vulnerable to freezing temperatures. Insauga.com reports residents with gardens or outdoor plants are being urged to take preventative measures, including covering cold-sensitive plants or moving them indoors where possible. The outlet notes frost can form on surfaces even when the measured air temperature stays slightly above 0 C, so gardeners and growers should take precautions regardless of the official reading.

items.title: Nearly 250 Residents Turn Out for Final Mayoral Debate in Port Credit and Lakeview Before Oct. 26 Vote
items.summary: Mississauga.com reports nearly 250 residents packed Christ First United Church on Lakeshore Road West on Oct. 15 for the final mayoral debate ahead of the city's Oct. 26 election. According to the outlet, the top four polling candidates, Bonnie Crombie, Dipika Damerla, Carolyn Parrish and Alvin Tedjo, were invited to the forum, co-hosted by the Town of Port Credit Association and the Lakeview Ratepayers Association. The outlet reports residents came out to hear how the candidates would address issues specific to the Lakeview and Port Credit communities, including safety, zoning and waterfront development. Mississauga.com says this marked the last scheduled debate before voters head to the polls later this month. The outlet notes all four candidates posed together for photos following the event.

items.title: Peel Police Ask Public to Help Find Missing 87-Year-Old Last Seen Driving From Mississauga's Summerville Area
items.summary: Peel Regional Police are asking for the public's help finding a missing 87-year-old man they describe as vulnerable, last seen in Mississauga early Friday afternoon. According to a police social media post shared Friday night, the man, identified as Keum-Sin, was last seen near Nawbrook Road and Dundas Street East in the Summerville area. Police say he left home driving a white 2020 Hyundai Elantra bearing Ontario licence plate CVZB364. The force describes Keum-Sin as a slim, five-foot-nine Asian man weighing about 165 pounds, balding with grey hair on the sides, brown eyes and no facial hair. Police say he was last seen wearing a beige spring jacket, black dress pants, a black and white baseball cap, burgundy dress shoes and eyeglasses. Officers say they are concerned for his well-being and are asking anyone with information to contact investigators.

items.title: Peel Municipalities Fall Behind Ford Government's Housing Targets as Affordability Gap Widens
items.summary: The Pointer reports Mississauga and Brampton now rank among the world's 15 least affordable places to buy a home, even as the province pushes municipalities to build more housing. According to the outlet, Ontario Premier Doug Ford assigned ambitious housing targets to 29 municipalities four years after his election, tasking Mississauga with 120,000 new homes by 2031 and Brampton with 113,000. The Pointer says that mandate was followed by sweeping legislative changes meant to accelerate development, many of which weakened environmental protections and eased restrictions on developers in the name of affordability. The outlet reports all three Peel municipalities are not on track to meet the housing goals the province set for them. The Pointer cites regional data showing 80 per cent of Peel residents cannot afford to buy a home.

items.title: Parole Board Upgrades Mississauga Man Zakaria Amara to Full Release Two Decades After Toronto Terror Plot
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Zakaria Amara, a Mississauga man who helped recruit members for a group that plotted to storm Parliament Hill and bomb several Toronto-area locations, has been granted full parole. According to the outlet, Amara had already spent four years on day parole under multiple conditions before the board upgraded his release after reviewing his case last week. The outlet says he was closely supervised during that period, with his internet use, friendships and relationships monitored, and no reported safety concerns or breaches. Insauga.com reports Amara remains barred from contacting anyone involved in criminal activity, including others arrested in the June 2006 anti-terrorist raids, or anyone holding extremist ideologies, except through his work as a consultant with a specialized program. The outlet says he must also keep participating in counselling and remain subject to financial monitoring and restrictions on his phone and internet use. Insauga.com notes the board's decision comes two decades after the dismantling of a homegrown plot that shocked the country and shifted public discourse around terrorism.

items.title: Mississauga Man Identified as Suspect in Yonge Street Attack on Pro-Palestinian Demonstrator
items.summary: Insauga.com reports a 20-year-old Mississauga man, Martin Salgatar, has been charged with aggravated assault after an alleged attack on a demonstrator during a pro-Palestinian rally in downtown Toronto. According to Toronto police, Salgatar surrendered to officers on Oct. 12, two days after the alleged assault near Yonge and Grosvenor streets on Saturday, Oct. 10. Investigators allege the victim was walking northbound on Yonge Street and talking with another demonstrator when the suspect approached from behind and punched the victim several times in the head without provocation. Police say the victim fell to the ground and sustained injuries to the face and leg. The outlet reports the Toronto Police Service's Hate Crime Unit is handling the investigation, which began with a public appeal for help identifying the suspect. Insauga.com says Salgatar was scheduled to appear at the Toronto Regional Bail Centre on Oct. 13.

items.title: House of the week: 3-storey semi-detached home with elevator in Mississauga
items.summary: This place: Three-storey semi-detached home with an elevator in Mississauga. Features: This semi-detached home offers over 4,400 square feet of living space with an elevator providing access to all floors. The main floor showcases tray ceilings, wide-plank light oak hardwood floors and expansive windows that fill the space with natural light. A marble fireplace anchors the living room. The kitchen features a large quartz island and high-end appliances. Glass doors lead to a landscaped backyard with a wood deck and a gas barbecue hookup. Upstairs, the primary bedroom has dual walk-in closets, an ensuite bathroom and a skylit hallway. Each additional bedroom includes walk-in closets and ensuite bathrooms. The third floor adds a flexible living space with two more bedrooms and a home office. The finished basement features a three-piece bathroom, a sauna and rough-ins for a second kitchen and laundry area. Additional highlights include a monitored smart home system, power blinds and an EV-ready epoxy garage. This home is steps away from Port Credit’s waterfront, boutique shopping, parks, dining, and it is also near GO Transit and the QEW.

items.title: Four Homes Razed as Edenshaw Breaks Ground on 30-Storey Port Credit Rental Tower
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Edenshaw Developments has broken ground on a 30-storey rental apartment building near the Port Credit GO Station in Mississauga, after demolishing four homes and a shed that previously occupied the site. According to the outlet, the project sits at 23 Elizabeth St. N. and 42-46 Park St., and a spokesperson for Edenshaw said demolition of the existing structures is nearly complete. The outlet reports the development has faced criticism before: a previous application for a 22-storey building on the same property was rejected by the Ontario Land Tribunal in 2023. Insauga.com says the height of the new 30-storey proposal remains a concern for some area residents. The outlet quotes a Facebook post from September in which a resident said surrounding buildings could be affected by privacy and overlook issues, shadow, wind, traffic, and construction dust and noise.
